articles.title: Referee hands out record 53 red cards after chaos at under-20s game in Brazil
articles.summary: Sendings-off include 43 players and two board members. Goal celebration is said to have sparked brawl. An under-20s match in the Brazilian state of Minas Gerais descended into chaos, with the referee handing out a record 53 red cards after a brawl.
body: The incident took place during the first leg of a state ⁠championship semi-final match between ⁠Uberlandia and ​Mamore. In his report the referee, Fernando Patrick Drosghic Modesto, said the trouble began early in the second half, ⁠when a number of Uberlandia officials invaded the field after one of their players was sent off.
The match was halted for 40 ⁠minutes and eventually restarted, with Mamore going on to score in the ninth minute of ​stoppage time to take a 3-1 lead.
According ‌to reports in Brazilian ‌media, the Mamore player Davi taunted Uberlandia players during the goal celebrations, which sparked a brawl and led to a deluge of red cards.
A total of 43 players and eight members of the coaching staff were sent off, and two Uberlandia board members were also dismissed.

articles.title: Britain's Stojsavljevic beaten in Hong Kong a day after landmark win
articles.summary: British teenager Mika Stojsavljevic was unable to back up her maiden WTA Tour win as she was knocked out in the last 16 of the Hong Kong Open.
body: Stojsavljevic, 17, shocked former Australian Open champion Sofia Kenin on Wednesday after being restored to the tournament as a lucky loser with only an hour's notice.
The Londoner was beaten 7-6 (7-5) 6-4 by Turkish world No 67 Zeynep Sonmez on Thursday in a little over two hours.
Stojsavljevic entered the Hong Kong Open ranked 411th in the world but is now just outside the top 350 in the live rankings following her victory over Kenin.
In 2024, she became the first Brit in 15 years to win the US Open girls' title, following Heather Watson's triumph back in 2009.

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo calls time on Portugal career after 234 caps and 146 goals
articles.summary: Player says that he will ‘hand back the No 7 shirt’ Ronaldo ended up falling out with Jorge Jesus. Cristiano Ronaldo has announced that he will not play for Portugal any more, ending an international career that spanned six World Cups and included a European title and the men’s all-time scoring…
body: The announcement marked the end of a lauded career that began more than two decades ago before Euro 2004 and finished with him walking out on the national team after falling out with coach Jorge Jesus.

“To the Portuguese people, the day has come for me to hand back the No 7 shirt of our national team,” the 41-year-old Ronaldo said in a long video message on social media. “I never felt it belonged to me alone but for 23 years I had the privilege and the responsibility of wearing it, defending it and carrying it with me into stadiums all around the world.

“Today the time has come to pass it on to the future. It was not an easy decision because some decisions are not made with the mind alone. They are also made with the heart. A journey that began in August 2003 and changed my life forever has come to an end.”

articles.title: Fifa wants to restrict women’s Olympic football to under-23s in controversial move
articles.summary: IOC open to dialogue and Fifa wants input from others. Fifa concerned about fixture congestion and workload. Fifa wants the International Olympic Committee to restrict the women’s Olympic football tournament to under-23s owing to concerns over fixture congestion and the workload of senior players.
body: The eligibility criteria for the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles has been set, with qualification tournaments having begun in some regions, so no change can be made until Brisbane 2032 at the earliest, but sources at both organisations have told the Guardian that they are open to dialogue.

Although no formal proposal has been made, Fifa is understood to be interested in examining the matter in talks with the IOC and other key stakeholders, such as the players and leading member associations whose national sides routinely qualify for the Games.
A move to bring in age restrictions would dramatically alter the nature of the event and require careful analysis, consultation and consideration through Fifa and IOC processes.

Such a change would be controversial and could provoke a backlash from leading international players because the Olympics has long been regarded as one of the highlights of the women’s calendar, with Emma Hayes’s United States team securing gold in Paris two years ago. The Olympic title has been contested eight times and the US have won five.

articles.title: Owono left out of Eq Guinea squad after death of De Miguel
articles.summary: Goalkeeper Jesus Owono will miss Equatorial Guinea's Afcon 2027 qualifiers after asking to be left out of the squad following the death of Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel.
body: De Miguel, 30, died after suffering a serious injury in a collision with Owono during a Spanish second division match on Monday.
Owono said he is experiencing "the most difficult days of my life" in a statement issued by his club FC Andorra on Wednesday, adding that it is "very hard to come to terms with what has happened".
Equatorial Guinea's football federation (Feguifut) said that the 25-year-old had requested to be left out of coach Vincenzo Alberto Annese's squad.
Feguifut president Venancio Tomas Micha had previously said his organisation was offering "all our human and professional backing" to the player.

articles.title: Man Utd unlikely to appoint interim should they sack Carrick
articles.summary: Manchester United are unlikely to appoint another interim head coach, Sky Sports News has been told, if they decide to replace Michael Carrick in the coming weeks.
body: There is still support for Carrick among the United hierarchy, and a lingering concern that changing the head coach won't necessarily change the team's fortunes.
The Champions League victory over Roma on Tuesday night has provided some respite, and boosted belief in the changing room and the boardroom. It was their first win in 10 matches in all competitions.

However, there is a realisation that one win on its own isn't enough to turn a season around. United remain 17th in the Premier League, only outside the relegation places on goal difference. And the nature of the victory against Roma was chaotic.

Whilst the character of the team to come back from 2-0 down suggests the players are still behind Carrick, it took a re-taken Bruno Fernandes penalty to turn the tide, and United's bosses still have doubts about the team's direction and lack of consistency.

articles.title: Wales opt for centre power pair against Japan
articles.summary: Wales head coach Steve Tandy has selected Max Llewellyn alongside Eddie James in midfield to face Japan in the Nations Championship on Saturday.
body: Wales head coach Steve Tandy has opted for power in his centre partnership by bringing in Max Llewellyn alongside Eddie James for the Nations Championship opener against Japan on Saturday (16:40 GMT).
Llewellyn, 6ft 6in (1.96m) and 16st 12lbs (107kg) and James, 6ft 4in (1.90m) and 16st 3lbs (103kg), will form one of Wales' biggest midfield combinations.
Tandy has abandoned his policy of selecting a more recognised ball-player at inside centre with Llewellyn named in the 12 jersey.
Fly-half Sam Costelow is preferred to Dan Edwards, while wings Josh Adams and Louis Rees-Zammit and full-back Blair Murray form the back three.

articles.title: Career-best Wembanyama display seals Spurs win
articles.summary: Victor Wembanyama sinks the winning free throw to finish with a career-high 52 points as the San Antonio Spurs beat the Dallas Mavericks 112-111.
body: The French star, whose previous best was 50 points in 2024, dominated at both ends of the court to also claim 24 rebounds and eight blocks.
The 22-year-old is the first player in 52 years with at least 50 points, 20 rebounds and five blocks in a game.
He also became the fifth player since 1982 to register at least 50 points and 20 rebounds as San Antonio improved their record to 6-2.
Wembanyama reached half-time with 29 points, 15 rebounds, five blocks and two steals, before the Spurs held off a second-half rally by Dallas, who were led by 29 points from Kyrie Irving.

articles.title: Another 'miracle' in Istanbul - but this one hurt Liverpool
articles.summary: Liverpool conceded "cheap" and "messy" goals in their defeat by Fenerbahce, says boss Andoni Iraola, as former Reds hero Dirk Kuyt celebrates a "miracle" in Istanbul.
body: When it comes to comebacks, Liverpool and Istanbul have plenty of history - but this time Andoni Iraola's side made the wrong kind.
Having hit the front for a second time against Fenerbahce, when Alexander Isak nodded in after 69 minutes, Liverpool were seemingly on their way to a thoroughly impressive away win.

But Iraola's players then capitulated amid a febrile atmosphere, as spirited hosts led by interim boss Dirk Kuyt - a Liverpool hero of years gone by - pulled off a shock Champions League comeback victory.

By losing 3-2 at the Sukru Saracoglu stadium, Iraola's visitors created that unwanted slice of history: this was the latest Liverpool have ever gone ahead in a major European game and then been beaten.

articles.title: NFL Week 9 injury report: Micah Parsons returns to Packers practice, Rams lose Jaylen Watson for season
articles.summary: Parsons has opened his 21-day practice window, while Jackson, Sam Darnold and Deshaun Watson headline the notable quarterback injuries entering Week 9
body: The 2026 NFL season is at the halfway point, Week 9, so that means some of the top players who have dealt with long-term injuries are ready to begin their returns to action.

Green Bay Packers coach Matt LaFleur told reporters that Micah Parsons ' 21-day practice window to return from the torn ACL and torn meniscus is now open. That means Parsons will begin practicing with the Packers for the first time this season, with the goal of returning for the Thanksgiving week game against the Los Angeles Rams.
"He put a lot of effort and work into this. Having him out there will be a big boost for our team," LaFleur said, via ESPN.
LaFleur also indicated Parsons will begin practicing as a limited participant in individual position drills while ramping him up to be full throttle in a couple of weeks.
